SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: SOIL AND ITS RESOURCES
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Soil and its resources helps you succeed in ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: SOIL AND ITS RESOURCES
Soil and its resources is part of Science learning. Connect every idea to something you can observe.
Use safe examples only. Do not try dangerous experiments without a teacher.
Write definitions in your own words, then add one drawing or real-life example.

PART 1: Identify parts of a plant immediate environment. Learners plants

What this means
In this part you learn to identify parts of a plant immediate environment. Learners plants. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify parts of a plant immediate environment. Learners plants.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Soil and its resources” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify parts of a plant immediate environment. Learners plants. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Draw different parts of a to observe parts of the plants plant from the immediate (roots, stem, leaves, flowers, fruits) environment from different types of plants

What this means
In this part you learn to draw different parts of a to observe parts of the plants plant from the immediate (roots, stem, leaves, flowers, fruits) environment from different types of plants. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: draw different parts of a to observe parts of the plants plant from the immediate (roots, stem, leaves, flowers, fruits) environment from different types of plants.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Say why Soil and its resources matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can draw different parts of a to observe parts of the plants plant from the immediate (roots, stem, leaves, flowers, fruits) environment from different types of plants. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Soil and its resources is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Soil and its resources” around your school. (skill: identify parts of a plant immediate environment. Learners plants)

Example 2: Say why Soil and its resources matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya. (skill: draw different parts of a to observe parts of the plants plant from the immediate (roots, stem, leaves, flowers, fruits) environment from different types of plants)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Soil and its resources to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify parts of a plant immediate environment. Learners plants.
3. Practise this skill: draw different parts of a to observe parts of the plants plant from the immediate (roots, stem, leaves, flowers, fruits) environment from different types of plants.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Soil and its resources from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Soil and its resources: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 2 learner study Soil and its resources?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Which type of soil soil types of soil using the soil samples provided (clay, loam, make good ribbons?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Soil and its resources means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify parts of a plant immediate environment. Learners plants.
5. Be able to: draw different parts of a to observe parts of the plants plant from the immediate (roots, stem, leaves, flowers, fruits) environment from different types of plants.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
